summary: Introductory security posture discovery focused on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options. Main concerns: KMS integration and key custody, SOC2 coverage and evidence, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC model compatibility, audit/log retention for legal/regulatory needs, and data residency. Agreed next steps include sharing SOC2 artifacts, scheduling a KMS deep dive, and prepping a Dedicated pilot quote.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on New Year's Eve, appreciate you carving time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. Jordan and Evan are with me, Jordan handles infra integrations. Can we do quick intros?
[00:08] Liam O'Neill: Yeah hi, Liam CTO at Borealis. We've been evaluating inference providers for our customer-facing assistants.
[00:12] Priya Desai: Priya, security lead. I'll focus on compliance and KMS.
[00:16] Carlos Mendez: Carlos, infra. I'll own the deployment stuff.
[00:19] Nadia Park: Nadia, product. I'm here for success criteria.
[00:22] Jordan Patel: Jordan, Redwood SE. I do deployments and KMS flows.
[00:26] Evan Ruiz: Evan, solutions eng — performance and benchmarking.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Cool. So agenda: quick run through of Borealis needs, then go over our security posture (SOC2, ISO where relevant), SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/encryption, audit logs, data retention, and then next steps.
[00:43] Liam O'Neill: High level: we're building a multi-tenant answers product that handles PII in some jurisdictions. Needs: data residency for EU customers, audit trail for compliance, and customer-managed keys for certain enterprise accounts. Also latency SLAs for premium tenants.
[00:57] Priya Desai: To add — we need to know what in-scope is for SOC2. Is inference hosted data stored? Where are logs kept? Can you redact or auto-delete?
[01:08] Maya Chen: Great questions. High level: Redwood hosted keeps minimal metadata by default, and we have optional KV/prefix caching that can be disabled. For enterprise accounts we recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, data isolation; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full network control.
[01:27] Priya Desai: Can you walk through KMS — BYOK? We have strict controls: keys must be in our AWS account or HSM and we need full key custody.
[01:36] Jordan Patel: Yep. For Dedicated we support BYOK via customer KMS in their account using cross-account roles and envelope encryption. For Private, you control the KMS entirely. Hosted can support tenant-level customer-managed keys but currently through a white glove onboarding — we can map that out.
[01:51] Carlos Mendez: When you say envelope encryption, is the model KV or cache data ever written encrypted-at-rest with our keys, or is it just the payload?
[02:00] Jordan Patel: The artifact — so the request payloads in transit are TLS, at rest we encrypt using the tenant's key for customer-managed keys, including caches we persist. But there are a few intermediate things: transient KV in GPU memory is ephemeral and not encrypted-at-rest, right — because it's in GPU RAM. We treat that as non-persistent.
[02:18] Priya Desai: That GPU RAM statement — we need it documented for our auditors. If data is in memory on shared hosts, we need assurance of isolation.
[02:25] Jordan Patel: Under Dedicated we guarantee no shared tenancy on GPUs with other customers. For hosted multi-tenant we rely on software isolation and KV sharding; it's in our SOC2 controls but we can send you the system description.
[02:37] Liam O'Neill: SOC2 scope — do you have Type II? What months and which components (control environment, change management, sys ops) are covered?
[02:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II for the control period Jan–Dec 2025 (we're in 2026 now) and the report includes the Redwood hosted API, control plane services, and our observability pipelines; Dedicated/Private are covered in parts for deployed code/config. We'll send the summary and system description.
[02:59] Priya Desai: Do you have ISO27001?
[03:02] Maya Chen: We are pursuing ISO27001, we have gap remediation ongoing; we can share the roadmap and any interim attestations.
[03:07] Nadia Park: On audit logs — our legal team may request 7 years retention for some regulated customers. Can you export logs and provide tamper-evident archives?
[03:16] Evan Ruiz: We can stream audit logs to customer-owned S3 or SIEM via syslog/connector — with signed delivery and immutable storage options (e.g., S3 Object Lock). Retention policy is configurable; long-term archival is supported but often part of our Enterprise package.
[03:31] Priya Desai: Good. What about RBAC — do you have SCIM integration and role mapping?
[03:35] Jordan Patel: Yes, SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO is supported for enterprise accounts. RBAC is flexible: we have built-in roles — Owner, Admin, Operator, ReadOnly — and you can create custom roles and map SCIM group attributes to roles. We also support session policies and token scoping.
[03:50] Liam O'Neill: How do API keys show up in audit logs? If a user rotates keys, can we tie activity to the user identity?
[03:55] Jordan Patel: We tag token usage with user metadata when SSO/SCIM users generate tokens — so logs include user id, session id, and request metadata. If someone uses a long-lived service key, it's attributed to the service account name.
[04:06] Priya Desai: Encryption in transit and at rest — what ciphers, TLS versions, and HSM provider?
[04:11] Evan Ruiz: TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred; we use AWS KMS for Hosted by default, but for BYOK we support customer KMS (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault) and external HSMs via PKCS#11 in Private deployments. We can provide cipher suite details in the security pack.
[04:27] Nadia Park: Data residency — can we pin EU customers to eu-north region?
[04:31] Maya Chen: Yes, we support region pinning for Dedicated and Private, and Hosted offers regional endpoints. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated in the target region or Private VPC deployment.
[04:40] Priya Desai: There's also the question of data deletion. We need timely deletion — e.g., delete customer data within 48 hours upon request for certain tenants. Is that supported?
[04:48] Jordan Patel: We have deletion APIs and retention policies. For hosted, deletion is asynchronous but SLA-backed for enterprise — we can commit to sub-72h for most artifacts, and for Dedicated/Private you control deletion. We'll surface specifics in the data handling doc.
[05:03] Liam O'Neill: On the compliance side, do you provide evidence like vulnerability scans, pen test reports, SOC2 audit trail extracts?
[05:10] Maya Chen: We provide redacted pen test summaries and vulnerability management evidence. Full raw reports are available under NDA. SOC2 sampling details can be provided as part of the security pack.
[05:21] Priya Desai: For BYOK — does Redwood ever see plaintext keys or get access to key material? That's a blocker for us if keys ever leave our control.
[05:29] Jordan Patel: Short answer: no, with BYOK we never store key material in plaintext. We use envelope encryption where our service gets a wrapped key; you hold the master KEK in your KMS. We can show a sequence diagram.
[05:40] Carlos Mendez: For Dedicated, how does network connectivity work — do we peer? Is it VPC peering, private link, or do you deploy into our VPC?
[05:48] Jordan Patel: We offer three patterns: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or customer-deployed nodes (our Private package) where Redwood-managed control plane talks to customer-hosted inference nodes over a secure management channel. We'll map options to your security needs.
[06:02] Nadia Park: Latency vs cost — one of our product KPIs is sub-200ms 95th for short prompts. Dedicated seems required for that. Any ballpark?
[06:10] Evan Ruiz: Sub-200ms is achievable on Dedicated with appropriate GPU class and model selection. We'll run an isolated benchmark with your representative prompt set; that way we can size the Dedicated pool.
[06:21] Liam O'Neill: Benchmarking — do you let customers run token-level cost and latency traces in a sandbox?
[06:26] Evan Ruiz: Yes, we provide per-token telemetry in the Console and can export traces. For pilots we give a telemetry token so you can run against a Dedicated shard and we collect traces for sizing.
[06:37] Priya Desai: A quick nitty gritty — audit log integrity. Can logs be signed server-side on write? Our auditors want proof logs aren't tampered with after the fact.
[06:46] Jordan Patel: We support write-once options with cryptographic signing and append-only storage; for Hosted we provide signed exports. For Dedicated/Private you can configure log forwarders to your SIEM with signatures.
[06:57] Maya Chen: Quick check — any regs we should be aware of? HIPAA? PCI?
[07:01] Priya Desai: We're not in PCI scope; HIPAA might apply for part of our dataset — we can clarify. Main focus is SOC2 + EU privacy.
[07:08] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include the privacy and HIPAA notes in the pack.
[07:11] Liam O'Neill: Who are your public reference enterprise customers for Dedicated/Private? For procurement we sometimes want references that had similar KMS requirements.
[07:19] Maya Chen: We can share anonymized case studies and 2 references under NDA — customers in fintech and health who used BYOK + dedicated deployments.
[07:28] Nadia Park: Any data residency limitations for model fine-tuning? We might want to fine-tune models on customer corpora and keep weights in region.
[07:35] Jordan Patel: Fine-tuning can be run on Dedicated or Private within a region; we can ensure artifacts (checkpoints) are stored in-region and encrypted with your keys.
[07:44] Priya Desai: For SCIM provisioning, do you support group nesting and custom claim mapping?
[07:48] Jordan Patel: Group nesting is partially supported; custom claims mapping is supported via attribute mapping in our SAML/SCIM console. There are some edge cases we can walk through in the next technical deep dive.
[07:59] Evan Ruiz: I'll own the benchmarking and region sizing follow-up — we'll need a sample prompt corpus and expected QPS.
[08:05] Carlos Mendez: I'll share our infra diagram and current KMS naming and key policies.
[08:09] Maya Chen: Okay next steps recap: we'll email the SOC2 summary and the private deployment checklist today, Jordan will prepare KMS sequence diagram and the SCIM/SAML detail, Evan will set up pilot telemetry instructions. Schedule a 60-min KMS + infra tech session early next week.
[08:28] Liam O'Neill: Sounds good. Any blockers on NDA for sharing pen test artifacts?
[08:32] Maya Chen: We'll circulate an NDA template; we can provide redacted summaries immediately and full docs post-NDA.
[08:37] Priya Desai: One last — backup and disaster recovery for Dedicated — RTO/RPO expectations?
[08:42] Jordan Patel: We aim for sub-1hr RTO for Dedicated controllers and sub-24hr RPO for persisted artifacts by default; we can tighten based on contract.
[08:52] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and a calendar invite for the KMS deep dive. Happy holidays.
[08:59] End of recording.

Notes: occasional transcription garble: 'KV' read as 'K V', 'BYOK' sometimes appears as 'BY OK'. References shared: security pack (link sent afterwards), SOC2 summary (link), Dedicated pilot pricing spreadsheet (internal link).
